problem: Consider the surface $z{e}^{x}+xy={x}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-1,1,2e).$
worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z{e}^{x}+xy & ={x}^{2} \\ z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,1,2e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(z{e}^{x}+y-2x)\text{ }i+x\text{ }j+{e}^{x}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,1,2e) & =((2e){e}^{-1}+1-2(-1))\text{ }i+(-1)\text{ }j+{e}^{-1}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i-j+{e}^{-1}\,k \\  & =⟨5,-1,{e}^{-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,1,2e)\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1,\,z-2e⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,-1,{e}^{-1}⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1,\,z-2e⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x+1)+(-1)(y-1)+{e}^{-1}(z-2e) & =0 \\ 5x-y+{e}^{-1}z+4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
